frequency_question: How often do executive principals with declared intent to strip a major institutional accreditor of federal recognition successfully complete the revocation within a presidential term window?
membership_rule: Members are cases where a cabinet-level department head formally moved to strip, withdraw, or terminate the recognition of a national accrediting body. Excluded are routine renewals, voluntary relinquishments, or mere investigative threats without formal administrative termination proceedings initiated.

cases.name: US Department of Education vs. American Bar Association (hypothetical/historical pressure points)
US Department of Education review of ACICS (American Council on Independent Colleges and Schools)
US Department of Education second review and final termination of ACICS

coverage_note: 3 named major accreditation termination battles involving federal education authorities since 1990.
known_gaps: Lower-level advisory committee recommendations that did not result in final departmental secretary action are excluded.
skeleton: Total department-level formal challenges to major recognized accreditor status resulting in termination proceedings.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 3 major historical challenges involving high-profile accreditors over 30 years.
validity_reason: Base rate tied to executive branch administrative behavior and political appointment cycles, which remain stable through current presidential administration.
